title: PAISE: PIM-Accelerated Inference Scheduling Engine for Transformer-based LLM
problem: LLM inference on GPUs is memory-bound due to the attention layer's low arithmetic intensity and high memory traffic from frequent KV-cache updates, leading to elevated latency under autoregressive token generation. GPU-only execution under-utilizes available bandwidth for attention operations.
motivation: As LLM context lengths and batch sizes grow, the KV-cache bandwidth bottleneck worsens, making GPU-only inference increasingly inefficient and prompting exploration of near-memory execution.
method: PAISE moves the memory-heavy attention computations (the parts where transformers multiply keys and values together) from an AMD MI100 GPU to HBM-PIM devices (special memory chips located near the GPU). A scheduling algorithm decides which operations to move based on the transformer's structure (layer type, number of attention heads) and the PIM hardware's capabilities (memory bandwidth and floating-point operations per second). The optimized code restructures the key-value cache data by spreading reads across multiple memory banks, so different attention heads can fetch their data simultaneously—this lets the hardware handle more memory requests in parallel.
key_novelty: PAISE's core innovation is moving transformer attention to specialized memory chips (PIM) by reorganizing data so multiple attention heads work in parallel, paired with a scheduling algorithm that picks which layers benefit most from this move.
contributions: A scheduling algorithm that selects which operations to offload to PIM based on model and hardware parameters.
An enhanced PIM GEMM kernel with interleave-batching and data layout optimization for attention.
Implementation and evaluation on GPT-2 and Llama2-7B using AMD MI100 + HBM-PIM.
Up to 48.3% reduction in execution time for attention layers vs GPU-only inference.

metrics.speedup: up to 48.3% execution time reduction vs GPU-only for attention layer

limitations: Evaluated only on GPT-2 and Llama2-7B; larger models and multi-GPU configurations are not assessed.
